title: Toll Transactions
how_it_works_companion: How It Works chapter 10, section HOW TOLL TRANSACTIONS WORK

sections.business_context:
Every car carries a toll tag, and the tolls arrive weeks later as a file from the toll authority, listing a tag,
a time, a place, and an amount. Somebody has to work out who was driving and recover the money.
This guide covers importing those transactions, matching them to trips, and recharging them to
members.
The problem it solves is small in each instance and large in aggregate. Individually a toll is a few
dollars; across a fleet across a year it is real money, and doing it by hand is the sort of task that
quietly stops being done.
Pairs with How It Works chapter 10, section HOW TOLL TRANSACTIONS WORK.

KEY COLUMNS ON VEHICLE_TOLL_TRANSACTION

Column                           Purpose

vehicle_id, toll_tag             Which car, and the tag the authority reported.

transaction_at                   When the toll was incurred. The key to matching.

toll_authority_code, location,
                                 Who charged it, where, and how much.
amount

member_charge_id                 The charge raised to recover it.
sections.implementation_workflow:
1) Importing a Batch
    1. Each branch’s region has its own toll authorities, resolved through
       TOLL_AUTHORITY_SELECT. A club operating in three markets deals with three sets of
       authorities, each with its own file format and its own reporting habits.
    2. Imports arrive on whatever cadence each authority supports - real time, daily, weekly, monthly,
       or a file somebody downloads by hand. This is deliberately open-ended. Do not build a fixed
       schedule or assume a single source: the import path must accept a batch whenever one
       arrives, from whichever authority, at whatever interval.
    3. Tolls reach the platform through the Zapier connector, configured by an administrator per
       authority. Where the authority offers a direct feed the connector reads it; where it publishes a
       downloadable report the administrator places that report where the connector picks it up. THE
       MAPPING FROM THE AUTHORITY’S COLUMNS INTO THE TOLL RECORD LIVES IN THE
       CONNECTOR, not in the platform - adding a city or an authority is configuration, not
       development.
    4. BRANCH_TOLL_SOURCE is the record of what is expected: which authority serves which
       branch, the integration_provider_id it arrives through, arrival_method, and
       expected_frequency. Stamp last_import_at and last_import_batch_id on every import. A feed
       that stops producing is otherwise indistinguishable from a month with no toll travel.
    5. Import from the batch the connector delivers, recording import_source and a batch identifier on
       every row.
    6. Resolve the tag to a vehicle. A tag that resolves to nothing is imported anyway, unmatched,
       rather than discarded, because a tag the club does not recognize is worth investigating.
    7. Do not import the same transaction twice. Deduplicate on the authority, the tag, and the
       timestamp.
    8. Set match_status to Unmatched on import. Matching is a separate step.

2) Matching to a Trip
    1. Find the trip for that vehicle whose actual window contains transaction_at. That is the match.
    2. Set vehicle_trip_id and move match_status to Matched.
    3. A toll falling outside every trip is a club movement or an anomaly. Leave it unmatched and
       surface it.
    4. A toll falling inside a service or internal trip is the club’s cost. Matched, but no member charge.
    5. A toll that should not be billed at all is marked excluded rather than Disputed - a staff
       repositioning run, an authority error. Excluded is the club’s decision that this is not a member’s
       to pay; disputed is a member’s contention still being resolved. Different facts, never collapsed.
    6. Match against actual trip times, never reservation times. A member who collected late did not
       incur a toll before they had the car.

EXAMPLE — WHAT A MATCH PRODUCES

Situation                     match_status     Charge raised

Inside a member trip          Matched          Yes, to that member

Inside a service trip         Matched          No; club cost
Situation                     match_status      Charge raised

Outside every trip            Unmatched         No; surfaced for review

Tag not recognized            Unmatched         No; surfaced for review

Member disputes it            Disputed          Held pending resolution



3) Recharging to the Member
    1. Every toll is captured individually and that list never collapses. One row per toll event, with its
       authority, place, timestamp and amount, for ever.
    2. Billing is the opposite. At billing time, sum all of a trip’s matched tolls and post a single
       member charge for the total - not one charge per toll. A member who drove through eight
       gantries on one weekend sees one toll line, not eight.
    3. Exclude Excluded and Disputed tolls from the sum. Only Matched tolls on a member trip are
       billed.
    4. Set member_charge_id on every toll in that group, pointing at the one charge. That is what lets
       the single statement line unfold back into the exact toll events behind it. The relationship is
       many tolls to one charge, which is why the column sits on the toll rather than the other way
       round.
    5. Describe the charge so a member recognizes it: the trip it covers and how many tolls, with the
       individual authority, place and date available behind it. A statement line reading only Toll will
       produce a telephone call.
    6. Any club markup on tolls is a commercial decision and belongs in the charge, not in the
       imported amount. Keep what the authority charged as the authority charged it.

4) Handling Disputes and Corrections
    1. A member disputing a toll moves the transaction to Disputed. The charge is not silently voided;
       somebody looks.
    2. Where the dispute succeeds, void the member charge with a reason. The transaction stays,
       matched, as the club’s cost.
    3. Where an authority reverses a toll, import the reversal rather than deleting the original.
    4. Never delete an imported transaction. The batch it came in is a record of what the authority
       said.

5) Working the Unmatched
    1. Unmatched transactions are the work. A queue of them, oldest first, is the screen that makes
       this feature earn its keep.
    2. Common causes: a toll during a gap between trips, a car moved without a trip recorded, a tag
       on a car sold months ago.
    3. Each of those is worth knowing about. The unmatched queue is a fleet diagnostic as much as
       a billing one.
    4. A transaction may be matched manually where the automatic match failed but a person can
       see the answer.
sections.rules_and_constraints:
1. Every imported transaction records its source and batch.
    2. Duplicates are prevented on authority, tag, and timestamp.
    3. A transaction whose tag resolves to no vehicle is imported unmatched, never discarded.
    4. Matching uses actual trip times, never reservation times.
    5. Every toll is captured individually and that list never collapses.
    6. Billing is aggregate: a trip’s matched tolls are summed into one member charge, never one
       charge per toll.
    7. Every toll in a billed group records the charge it was billed under.
    8. Excluded and Disputed tolls are left out of the sum.
    9. Excluded means the club has decided it is not a member’s to pay; disputed means a member
       is contesting it.
    10. Toll authorities are per region and imports arrive on whatever cadence each supports; no fixed
        schedule is assumed.
    11. A toll inside a service or internal trip is the club’s cost.
    12. The imported amount is what the authority charged; any markup lives in the charge.
    13. A disputed toll is held for review rather than voided automatically.
    14. A reversal is imported; the original is never deleted.
    15. No imported transaction is ever deleted.
sections.integration_and_edge_cases:
1. A toll two minutes after check-in. Outside the trip, so unmatched. Usually the member
       driving away from the branch in their own car, and usually the club’s to absorb, but a person
       should decide.
    2. A toll during a gap between two member trips. The club moved the car. Unmatched,
       surfaced, and almost always a club cost.
    3. A tag on a car the club sold. Should not happen and does. The unmatched queue is how it is
       discovered, and the answer is to return the tag.
    4. A member disputing a toll they did incur. Disputed, reviewed, and either upheld or written
       off. The transaction stays either way.
    5. A batch imported twice. Deduplication catches it. Without the check, every member is
       charged twice and the club finds out from complaints.
    6. A toll on a shared package. Charged to the member who drove, which is the participant on
       the trip, not necessarily the primary.
    7. An authority reversing a toll months later. Imported as its own transaction and reconciled
       against the original.
    8. Tolls arriving after a member has left the club. The charge is still theirs and the club
       decides whether to pursue it. The record does not become somebody else’s.
sections.automations_and_notifications:
Each automation below is listed with its trigger and its expected outcome. Operational specification is
reserved for the automations pass that follows the first draft of all chapters.


AUTOMATIONS IN THIS GUIDE

Trigger                         Outcome

Batch imported                  Transactions created; duplicates rejected; tags resolved to vehicles.

Matching run                    Transactions matched to trips by vehicle and time.

Match to a member trip          Dollar charge raised to that member, linked back.

Transaction unmatched           Added to the review queue.

Member disputes a toll          Status set to Disputed; charge held pending review.

Unmatched queue growing         Surfaced to staff.


Reserved for the automations pass: import schedule and source configuration, the matching tolerance
around trip boundaries, and how long a disputed toll is held.
sections.developer_notes:
1. Capture individually, bill in aggregate. These pull in opposite directions and both are right:
       the detail is the record, the charge is what a member reads. One charge per toll produces a
       statement nobody can use; one row per charge destroys the ability to answer which gantry.
    2. Deduplicate on import. Authority, tag, and timestamp. A double import charges every
       member twice and the club hears about it from members rather than from the system.
    3. Import first, match second. Two separate steps. Combining them means a matching failure
       loses the transaction, which is the one thing that must not happen.
    4. Match on actual times. Reservation times would charge a member for a toll incurred before
       they had the car.
    5. Never discard an unresolvable row. An unrecognised tag is information. Import it
       unmatched and let somebody look.
    6. Keep the authority amount pure. Whatever the club adds belongs in the charge. Mixing
       them makes reconciliation against the authority impossible.
    7. The unmatched queue is a feature. Build it as a working screen rather than an error log,
       because it is where cars moved without trips and tags on sold cars get discovered.
    8. Never delete. Reversals are transactions. The batch record is what lets a bad import be
       unwound.
sections.testing_checklist:
Import
    ☐ Every imported transaction records its source and batch.
    ☐ Importing the same batch twice creates no duplicates.
    ☐ A tag resolving to no vehicle is imported unmatched.
    ☐ Transactions are created with a status of Unmatched.

Matching
    ☐ A toll inside a member trip window is matched to that trip.
    ☐ Matching uses actual trip times rather than reservation times.
    ☐ A toll inside a service trip is matched and raises no member charge.
    ☐ A toll outside every trip stays unmatched and appears in the queue.
    ☐ A transaction can be matched manually.

Charging and Disputes
    ☐ A trip with several matched tolls produces one member charge for their total.
    ☐ Every toll in that group records the same member_charge_id.
    ☐ The single charge unfolds back into the individual toll events.
    ☐ An excluded toll is not included in the billed total.
    ☐ A disputed toll is not included in the billed total.
    ☐ A toll marked Excluded is distinguishable from one marked Disputed.
    ☐ The charge description names the authority, place, and date.
    ☐ The imported amount is unchanged by any club markup.
    ☐ A disputed toll holds the charge rather than voiding it.
    ☐ An upheld dispute voids the charge with a reason and keeps the transaction.
    ☐ A reversal is imported as its own transaction.
    ☐ No imported transaction can be deleted.
